routes.label: Verify a closed form by induction

solution:
Taking base-\(7\) logarithms turns the exponents in the defined operations into multiplication and division. The resulting recurrence has consecutive factors that cancel.

All terms \(a_n\) are positive, since the recursion repeatedly raises positive numbers to real powers. Define
\[
b_n=\log_7(a_n).
\]
The initial value is
\[
b_3=\log_7\left(3^{1/\log_7 2}\right)
=\frac{\log_7 3}{\log_7 2}.
\]
For \(n\ge4\), substituting the two operation rules gives
\[
a_n=\left(n^{1/\log_7(n-1)}\right)^{\log_7(a_{n-1})}
=n^{b_{n-1}/\log_7(n-1)}.
\]
Thus
\[
b_n=\frac{\log_7 n}{\log_7(n-1)}\,b_{n-1}.
\]
Iterating this relation produces the telescoping product
\[
b_{2019}
=\frac{\log_7 2019}{\log_7 2018}
\cdot\frac{\log_7 2018}{\log_7 2017}
\cdots
\frac{\log_7 4}{\log_7 3}
\cdot\frac{\log_7 3}{\log_7 2}
=\frac{\log_7 2019}{\log_7 2}.
\]
Every internal logarithm cancels, and the change of base formula identifies the result as \(\log_2 2019\).

To justify rounding without a calculator, note that
\[
2^{10.5}=1024\sqrt2<1536<2019<2048=2^{11},
\]
where \(\sqrt2<3/2\). Therefore
\[
10.5<\log_2 2019<11.
\]
The nearest integer is \(\boxed{11}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The first term is a fixed power of \(3\). This suggests that every \(a_n\) might be the same fixed power of its index, with the logarithms in the recursion canceling to preserve that exponent.

Set
\[
c=\frac1{\log_7 2}.
\]
We will prove \(a_n=n^c\) for every integer \(n\ge3\). The initial condition gives \(a_3=3^c\), so the claim holds at the starting index.

Suppose it holds at index \(n-1\), so that \(a_{n-1}=(n-1)^c\). Substituting into the defining operations,
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_n
&=\left(n^{1/\log_7(n-1)}\right)^{\log_7((n-1)^c)}\\
&=n^{\frac{c\log_7(n-1)}{\log_7(n-1)}}\\
&=n^c.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(n-1\ge3\), so the logarithm in the denominator is nonzero. This proves the formula by induction.

It follows that
\[
\log_7(a_{2019})
=c\log_7 2019
=\frac{\log_7 2019}{\log_7 2}
=\log_2 2019.
\]
Since \(\sqrt2<3/2\),
\[
2^{10.5}=1024\sqrt2<1536<2019<2048=2^{11}.
\]
Thus the logarithm is between \(10.5\) and \(11\), and its nearest integer is \(\boxed{11}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutionMethods.label: Find a fixed-power formula
